subject: Clarify session token "waterfall" and EOM spike on invoice
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@stellahealth.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@stellahealth.io>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected token spike on July 31 invoice — please advise

Hi Sean / Naomi,

We noticed a large jump in billed tokens that landed on our July 31 invoice (invoice #ST-20260731). Our internal telemetry shows a steady client-side request rate, but Redwood's metering shows a short 11:45–11:50 PM UTC spike that multiplied tokens by ~4x for several sessions. That window pushed us over our committed tier and created an overage charge plus VAT that we did not expect.

Can you provide per-request metering logs and a short explanation for what your "waterfall" counting is for streaming responses? Our finance team needs evidence for VAT reclassification and to decide whether to accept the overage charge.

Attachments: stella_eom_invoice_20260801.pdf

Appreciate urgent help — we're on a tight close window.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
CFO, Stella Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@stellahealth.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token spike on July 31 invoice — please advise

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the invoice. We're looking into the 11:45–11:50 PM UTC window now. Preliminary notes:

- We will export per-request meter-level logs (request id, model variant, token_in/token_out, stream fragments) for that 10-minute window and share a CSV.
- The term we use internally, "token waterfall", refers to how streaming responses are counted when partial chunks are emitted plus subsequent re-sends from client reconnects. In edge cases that can multiply billed tokens if a client reconnects repeatedly and we conservatively bill full output per distinct stream fragment.
- We also want to check whether your client retried with slightly different prompt prefixes — retries can produce repeated output that gets billed.

Action plan: Naomi will pull the logs and Karthik will run a quick aggregation to show how counts map to billed units. We'll aim to get initial logs to you by EOD (your timezone). If there is clear double-counting due to reconnect semantics on our side, we'll propose a pro-rated credit and fix the counting heuristics.

Best,
Sean
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: request-logs-export-stub (will follow)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: logs request — pulling CSV and quick QC

Karthik — forwarding Marta's note. I'm pulling the per-request dump for 2026-07-31 23:30–00:05 UTC and attaching a sample CSV extract for the spike window (2026-08-09-stella-usage-sample.csv). Please run the aggregation by (a) request id, (b) client session id, and (c) stream fragment sequence. If we see repeated output for the same session id caused by reconnects, mark those rows.

If it's our conservative fragment billing that caused the issue, propose a credit equal to the duplicate token volume (estimate now: ~29,400 tokens) and flag for ops to tweak streaming billing heuristics.

Naomi
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-08-09-stella-usage-sample.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@stellahealth.io>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token spike on July 31 invoice — analysis and next steps

Marta / team — thanks for waiting. Quick summary of what we found from the 23:45–23:50 UTC window:

- Root cause: three client reconnects from the same session id caused the service to emit the final stream fragment each time. Our current billing rule charges each distinct stream fragment emission as output tokens.
- Evidence: exported CSV shows identical output chunk text and token counts for request ids r_78342, r_78343, r_78344 with matching session id s_ab12. I attached the small sample extract for transparency.
- Impact: of the ~184k tokens billed in that window, ~32k are duplicates attributable to reconnects.

Proposed remediation:
1) Immediate: apply a one-time credit of 32,000 tokens (value shown on a pro-rated basis in a credit memo) to your August invoice; we will also reverse the VAT on that portion in the EU region per tax guidance once the credit posts.
2) Short term: ops will update the billing pipeline to deduplicate consecutive identical fragment emissions within a 60s window per session id (rollout target: 2 weeks).
3) We'll provide the per-request CSV and a reconciliation spreadsheet for your finance team.

Next steps: Sean will open a HubSpot ticket and Naomi will issue the credit memo. Expect the CSV and ticket link within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Metering & Billing
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: reconciliation-spreadsheet (shared link sent separately)
